summary: Aries rising is classically read as a lean, quick, combative and self-willed person, brave but hot-tempered and restless. For this lagna the Sun and Jupiter are the main helpers, Mars as lagna lord supports them, and Saturn, Mercury and Venus are counted as difficult; Venus is the main maraka.
common_outcomes: Brave, enterprising and independent, with a quick temper and a dislike of being directed (PD 9.1; JP 9.104; HJH; Frawley).
Restless or always on the move (PD 9.1: always on his legs; JP 9.104: wandering habits).
Lean or middle stature, round eyes, weak knees noted by Phaladeepika and Jataka Parijata; Raman adds a long face and neck and a mark or scar on the head.
Liable to cuts, bruises and wounds and to complaints of the head when Aries is afflicted (PD 9.1; BR Mesha st. 5; HJH).
rare_outcomes: Bhavartha Ratnakara (Mesha st. 22): baths in the Ganges in the periods of Venus, Jupiter and the Sun if all three are in the 10th.
Jataka Parijata 9.104: hostile to relatives and of uncertain wealth.
Raman: mental strain is possible if Saturn and the Moon are both in Aries (HJH ch. IV).

by_area.personality: Fierce, proud, quick-tempered and quarrelsome yet heroic (JP 9.104); fickle and impatient (PD 9.1); independent, courageous, ambitious, stubborn but frank, goes to extremes (HJH); dynamic, competitive, lives in the head, strategic, can be self-centred (Frawley p. 117).
by_area.career: Enterprising, able to plan, drawn to scientific thought (HJH); good at research, invention and new ideas (Frawley p. 117).
by_area.finance: Possessed of uncertain wealth (JP 9.104). Self-earned fortune if Mars and Venus are in the 7th (BR Mesha st. 15); the Sun, Mercury and Venus in the 11th give fortune in their periods (BR Mesha st. 20).
by_area.health: Fear of eruptive fevers (smallpox), weapons and wounds (BR Mesha st. 5); bruised limbs (PD 9.1); head complaints when Aries is afflicted and a hot constitution (HJH); Mercury and Mars in the 6th give wounds and skin eruptions in their periods (BR Mesha st. 14).
by_area.relationships: Longs for women (PD 9.1); Frawley says Aries types benefit from relationships to balance their self-focus (p. 117).
by_area.family: Hostile to relatives (JP 9.104). Raman notes Parasara and Lomasa hold that the lagna lord in the 5th gives little happiness from children (BR Mesha notes to st. 12).
by_area.spirituality: Frawley: growth comes from using a sharp mind to seek truth rather than to promote oneself (p. 117).

strengtheners: Bhavartha Ratnakara: the lords of the 4th and 5th (Moon and Sun) together give Raja Yoga (Mesha st. 1); the Sun or Moon in Cancer gives Raja Yoga (st. 21); the Sun aspected by Jupiter becomes a yogakaraka (st. 19).
The 2nd lord in the 12th is good only for Aries, because Venus is then exalted in Pisces (BR Mesha st. 7 and Raman's note).
Mars becomes a yoga-giver in the 2nd with Jupiter and Venus (st. 9), in the 4th with Jupiter (st. 11; Raman: neecha-bhanga) and in the 5th (st. 12).
Jupiter-Sun, Jupiter-Mars or Mars-Sun links are highly favourable for Aries (Santhanam's note on BPHS 34.19-22); Laghu Parashari notes list Sun+Mars, Sun+Moon, Mars+Jupiter as fruitful (Verma).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter and Saturn together (9th and 10th lords) do not give Raja Yoga because Saturn also owns the 11th (BPHS 34.19-22; LP Aries vv.; BR Mesha st. 4; HPA).

Jupiter gives bad results if under the control of a malefic (BPHS 34.19-22); Jupiter in the 11th gives no yoga in its period (BR Mesha st. 13); Jupiter in the 10th (debilitated) can act as a maraka (BR Mesha st. 3).
Mars in the 3rd with Jupiter and Venus gives no yoga (BR Mesha st. 10); Mars in the 8th gives no yoga by itself (st. 16).
Mars joined with the 6th lord can bring death through head disease in its period (BR Mesha st. 6) [maraka: text predicts danger to life / death].
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
lagna_or_context_notes: For Aries the 9th lord Jupiter also owns the 12th and the 10th lord Saturn also owns the 11th, so the 9-10 combination is spoiled; the cleaner Raja Yoga for Aries comes from the Sun (5th) with the Moon (4th) or with Mars or Jupiter.

Sun (BPHS 34.19-22; LP; HJH; HPA; PVR)

source_views.view: Aries rising gives round eyes, weak knees, fierceness, fear of water, sparing diet, restlessness, fickleness and bruised limbs; Aries is movable, cruel, male, abode a forest.

Raman's notes: Keraleeya names Mercury and Saturn as marakas; in his experience several Aries natives died in Venus dasa.

source_views.view: Jupiter best benefic, then Mars; Saturn, Mercury and Venus malefic, Mercury the worst. Aries rising: courageous, independent, enterprising, quick-tempered; head troubles if afflicted.

source_views.view: Saturn, Mercury and Venus ill-disposed; Jupiter and Sun auspicious; Jupiter the yogakaraka; Jupiter-Saturn gives no benefit; Venus as maraka will not kill but Saturn and similar planets can.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, pp. 117, 161
source_views.view: Aries types are dynamic, competitive, strategic and headstrong; for Aries and Scorpio, Raja Yoga comes from the Sun with the Moon.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, sec. 13.2, Table 30
source_views.view: Functional benefics Sun, Mars, Jupiter; malefics Mercury, Venus, Saturn; no yogakaraka; Moon not listed for movable lagnas.

disagreements: Venus as killer: BPHS 34 makes Venus an independent killer; Raman (BR notes) reports Parasara and Keraleeya saying Venus alone cannot kill, and HPA says Venus as maraka will not kill; Verma rejects that reading as corrupt; Raman's own experience is that Aries natives have died in Venus dasa. Jupiter: auspicious in BPHS, Raman's yogakaraka in HPA, but a maraka in the 10th per Bhavartha Ratnakara. Mercury vs Saturn as worst malefic: HJH names Mercury; Santhanam's note on BPHS stresses Saturn's 11th (moolatrikona) lordship. Moon: BPHS silent; Verma counts a weak Moon auspicious.
phrasing_guidance: Describe the rising sign as a tendency, not a fixed fate; blend it with planets in the 1st house, the lagna lord and the Moon sign. Name functional roles plainly (e.g. 'Saturn tends to work in your favour') and never turn maraka lore into a death or illness prediction; skip old caste, gender and fidelity stereotypes from the classical lists.

summary: Taurus rising is classically read as a steady, enduring, pleasure-loving and generous person, attached to land, cattle, comfort and beauty, and happier in the middle and later parts of life. Saturn (9th and 10th lord) is the yogakaraka for most authorities, while Jupiter, the Moon and Venus are counted as difficult.
common_outcomes: Patient and enduring; bears hardship and forgives (PD 9.2; HJH; Frawley).
Fond of comfort, beauty, music and pleasure (PD 9.2; HJH; Frawley).
Linked with agriculture, cattle and property (PD 9.2; JP 9.104; Frawley p. 118).
Obstinate and slow to move once committed (HJH; Frawley).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 9.2: marks or moles on the back, face or sides.
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Vrishabha st. 2): Rahu in the 10th, or Mars and Jupiter in Capricorn, gives baths in sacred rivers.
Raman: nervous complaints are common after about fifty (HJH ch. IV).

by_area.personality: Forgiving, liberal, enduring, fond of young women (PD 9.2); respectful to elders and Brahmanas, fond of debate, wandering, fortunate, calm (JP 9.104); obstinate, proud, ambitious, open to flattery but affectionate, self-reliant, with a piercing intellect and great endurance (HJH); stable, fixed, sensual, possessive, slow to anger and slow to forgive (Frawley p. 118).
by_area.career: Agriculture (PD 9.2); business, banking or property, artistic and poetic work (Frawley p. 118); sees himself as born to exercise authority (HJH).
by_area.finance: Plenty of wealth in Venus dasa (BR Vrishabha st. 13); Jupiter and Mercury joined or in mutual aspect give Dhana Yoga, spoiled if Mars joins or aspects (st. 5-6); the Moon in the lagna reduces wealth (st. 14); Mars dasa gives financial gain (st. 8).
by_area.health: Plump thighs and a large face (PD 9.2); Raman: stout or corpulent tendency and nervous complaints after fifty (HJH).
by_area.relationships: Fond of young women (PD 9.2); lustful (JP 9.104); values marriage and a stable home, romantic (Frawley p. 118).
by_area.family: Few sons (JP 9.104); not much happiness from children (HJH).
by_area.spirituality: Pays homage to elders and Brahmanas (JP 9.104); devotional, drawn to tradition and ritual (Frawley p. 118).

strengtheners: Saturn alone gives Raja Yoga (BPHS 34.23-24; LP Taurus vv. 47-48; HPA); Raman (after B. Suryanarayana Rao) says Saturn is best in the 10th (BR notes).
Mercury joining Saturn or the Sun acts more effectively (Santhanam's note on BPHS 34.23-24); Saturn + Mercury is the best yoga for Taurus (Verma's LP note).
The Moon in the 4th, or aspected by Jupiter or Mercury, can give yoga (BR Vrishabha st. 3).
Mars in the 7th becomes benefic (BR Vrishabha st. 4); Jupiter, Mercury and Mars linked together become yoga-givers (st. 7); Mercury in a kendra gives yoga in its period (st. 8).
Venus and Mercury in the lagna with Jupiter in the 7th gives a powerful yoga in Mercury dasa (BR Vrishabha st. 9).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter, 8th and 11th lord, is the first-rate adversary (Santhanam's note on BPHS 34.23-24).
The Dhana Yoga of Jupiter and Mercury fails if Mars joins or aspects them (BR Vrishabha st. 6).
The Moon in the lagna does not give much wealth for Taurus, though it helps other lagnas (BR Vrishabha st. 14-15).
Raman/Suryanarayana Rao: Saturn may give Raja Yoga without letting the native hold on to the gains; Saturn in the 2nd is destructive (BR notes).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
lagna_or_context_notes: Saturn owns the best trine (9th) and the best angle (10th) for Taurus, hence its reputation as the strongest yogakaraka of the zodiac (Santhanam; Verma). Venus as lagna lord also owns the 6th (its moolatrikona Libra), which is why several texts do not count it as a benefic.

description_by_source.description: Stable, enduring, fixed; sense of form and beauty; possessive and materialistic; good memory; values marriage and home; devotional.

yogakaraka: Saturn, 9th and 10th lord (BPHS 34.23-24; LP; HJH; HPA; PVR; Raman, HJH ch. II p. 15) - but Bhavartha Ratnakara (Vrishabha st. 1) denies it
functional_benefics: Saturn (all except BR)
Sun, 4th lord (BPHS 34.23-24 auspicious; HJH; PVR; Laghu Parashari editions differ: auspicious or neutral)
Mercury, 2nd and 5th lord (BPHS: somewhat auspicious; LP: auspicious; HJH; PVR)
Mars per HJH only (owner of 7th and 12th)

Venus, lagna and 6th lord (BPHS; LP; HPA; PVR); HJH says Venus may be neutral as lagna lord

source_views.view: Yogakaraka Saturn; functional benefics Sun, Mercury, Saturn; neutral Mars; malefics Moon, Jupiter, Venus (table layout as printed in the copy read).

Venus: malefic in BPHS, LP, HPA, PVR; neutral in HJH; Susloka Sataka (cited by Santhanam) says the 6th lordship does not taint Venus here. Sun: auspicious in BPHS and HJH; neutral in some LP readings. Mars: benefic (HJH), neutral (PVR, Verma), killer (BPHS).

summary: Gemini rising is classically read as a quick, sociable, talkative and pleasure-loving person, good at reading others, fond of music and learning, but restless and changeable. Venus (5th lord) is the one clearly good planet; Mars, Jupiter and the Sun are counted as difficult; there is no single-planet yogakaraka.
common_outcomes: Clever, quick-witted, fond of reading, writing and talk (HJH; Frawley).
Liking for music and dance (PD 9.3); voluptuous and fond of relatives (JP 9.105).
Skilled at reading others' thoughts (PD 9.3).
Nervous, restless and changeable; can exhaust itself (HJH; Frawley).
rare_outcomes: Jataka Parijata 9.105: exceedingly prosperous, contemplative and philosophical, but ailing.
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Mithuna st. 10): Mercury in the 11th brings misunderstandings with the eldest brother.
Frawley p. 118: tends to marry more than once.

by_area.personality: Dark eyes, curly hair, raised nose, home-keeping, playful (PD 9.3); compassionate, worthy, contemplative, liked by the good (JP 9.105); wavering mind, ingenious, vivacious, inconsistent (HJH); restless, adaptable, articulate, can be unreliable or tricky (Frawley p. 118).
by_area.career: Experts in mechanical sciences, conversation and literature, best in active work (HJH); writers, journalists, secretaries, programmers, scientists (Frawley p. 118).
by_area.finance: Venus, Mars and the Moon in the 2nd give wealth in Venus dasa (BR Mithuna st. 2); the Moon and Mars in the 11th with Saturn in the 9th give strong Dhana Yoga (st. 8); Mars and Saturn in the 2nd with the Moon in the 8th lose wealth in their periods (st. 5-6).
by_area.health: Ailing (JP 9.105); prone to sudden nervous breakdown (HJH); weak but active, can be hypersensitive (HJH; Frawley).
by_area.relationships: Sporting with women (PD 9.3); voluptuous (JP 9.105); should be careful with the opposite sex (HJH); mobile in relationships, may marry more than once (Frawley p. 118).
by_area.family: Fond of relatives (JP 9.105); home-keeping (PD 9.3); misunderstanding with the eldest brother if Mercury is in the 11th (BR Mithuna st. 10).
by_area.spirituality: Knows the real nature of the world and spirit, contemplative (JP 9.105); can become quite spiritual once seeking inner knowledge (Frawley p. 119).

strengtheners: Venus with Mercury gives Raja Yoga (LP Gemini notes; HPA); Venus with Saturn in good signs gives a distinguished career (HPA).
The Sun and Mercury in the 3rd make Mercury give yoga in its period (BR Mithuna st. 1).
Saturn's 9th lordship (moolatrikona) outweighs its 8th lordship (Santhanam's notes on BPHS 34.2-7); Saturn-Mercury links give Raja Yoga (Verma).
Santhanam suggests a Saturn-Jupiter exchange between the 9th and 10th could be favourable for Gemini (his own view, note on BPHS 34.25-26).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).

Attached to home, family and friends; many houses or dwells in others' homes (PD 9.4; JP 9.105; HJH; Frawley).

strengtheners: Mars, owner of the 5th and 10th, gives full yoga (BPHS 34.27-28; LP; HJH; HPA; PVR; BR Karkataka st. 2).

Venus in the 12th or 2nd gives yoga (BR Karkataka st. 3); Mercury and Venus in the 12th give Raja Yoga in Venus dasa (st. 9); Mercury and Venus in the 5th make Mercury give yoga (st. 5).

Jupiter with Venus, or Jupiter with Saturn, are spoilt combinations (Verma).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
lagna_or_context_notes: For movable lagnas the 11th lord is a strong malefic: Venus for Cancer (Santhanam's note on BPHS 34.27-28). The Moon as lagna lord is the least of the three benefics (Mars, Jupiter, Moon) in Santhanam's ranking.

summary: Leo rising is classically read as proud, brave and commanding, quick to anger, drawn to forests, hills and travel, and able to overcome enemies and charm rulers. Mars (4th and 9th lord) is the yogakaraka and the best planet; the Sun and Jupiter are also good; Mercury, Venus and Saturn are counted as difficult.

by_area.relationships: Longs for women (JP 9.106); does not always do well in partnership, may dominate partners (Frawley p. 120).
by_area.family: Few sons (JP 9.106); obedient to the mother (PD 9.5); may hold children too tightly (Frawley p. 120).
by_area.spirituality: Orthodox in religion yet tolerant, some philosophical knowledge (HJH); can develop greatness of soul when pride is controlled (Frawley p. 120).

lagna_or_context_notes: Virgo is a biped sign, strong as lagna (Brihat Jataka 1.17). Mercury rules both the lagna and the 10th, so its strength matters doubly.

Saturn (4th and 5th lord) is the yogakaraka; Mercury is also good; Jupiter, the Sun and Mars are counted as difficult; Venus is neutral.

by_area.family: Limited number of children (PD 9.7). The Sun and Mercury in the 12th aspected by Saturn: father fortunate but lives to middle age (BR Thula st. 5).
by_area.spirituality: Worships gods and Brahmins (PD 9.7); can transcend the world through love of truth (Frawley p. 121).

Libra is a biped sign, strong as lagna (Brihat Jataka 1.17).

summary: Capricorn rising is classically read as hard-working, persistent and strong-willed, finishing what it starts, practical and ambitious, though sometimes lazy, shameless or prone to wind complaints. by_area.relationships: Fond of women (PD 9.10; JP 9.108); perfectionist at home, may not get on with the spouse (HJH).

Phaladeepika's harsher traits (hypocrisy, shamelessness) should not be repeated to a user.

summary: Aquarius rising is classically read harshly - secretive, covetous, careful with money, with fluctuating gains and losses - while Raman and Frawley describe a reserved, humanitarian, intelligent person suited to teaching, writing and service. Venus (4th and 9th lord) is the yogakaraka and Saturn is good; Jupiter, the Moon and Mars are counted as difficult.
common_outcomes: Reserved, sympathetic and helpful to others (HJH; Frawley).
Fluctuating gains and losses; careful or miserly with money (PD 9.11; JP 9.109).
Endures long journeys (PD 9.11).
Shines as teacher, writer, speaker (HJH).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 9.11: body shaped like a water-pot; fond of perfumes and flowers.
Raman: setbacks that can affect reputation unless other factors help (HJH).
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Kumbha st. 6): the Sun, Mercury and Jupiter in the 3rd give political power through the Sun.

by_area.personality: Secretly does wrong, covetous, uses others' wealth (PD 9.11); crafty, miserly (JP 9.109); reserved, peevish when provoked but quick to calm, generous, very sympathetic, intelligent, good memory, sometimes timid (HJH); self-effacing, humanitarian, may be eccentric (Frawley p. 124).
by_area.career: Teachers, writers, lecturers, astrology, upholders of causes (HJH); religious leaders and teachers rather than political leaders (Frawley p. 124); Frawley notes Aquarius is sometimes called the worst ascendant for fame and charisma (p. 162).
by_area.finance: Limited means, gains and losses (PD 9.11); master of much wealth (JP 9.109). Venus and Saturn in the 11th give yoga in Venus dasa (BR Kumbha st. 5).
by_area.health: Colic and chest pain (HJH); a weak chest if Saturn is in the 4th (HJH).
by_area.relationships: Fond of other men's wives (JP 9.109); devoted to the spouse, needs a happy home or health suffers, family happiness not sufficient (HJH).
by_area.spirituality: Frawley: often called the best sign for spiritual growth, capable of surrender to the Divine (pp. 124, 162).

strengtheners: Venus, owner of the 4th and 9th, is the only Raja Yoga planet (BPHS 34.41-42; LP; HJH; HPA; PVR; Frawley).
Venus with Mars (9th and 10th lords) gives Raja Yoga (LP; HPA); best if Venus is in the 10th and Mars in the 9th (Verma). Raman holds the 9-10 combination works in practice (BR notes).
Venus in the lagna, the Sun in the 10th and Rahu in Aquarius give yoga in Rahu and Jupiter dasas (BR Kumbha st. 2).
Jupiter aspecting the 2nd and Saturn aspecting the lagna (each its own house) help finances in both periods (Raman's note on BR Kumbha st. 4).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Bhavartha Ratnakara (Kumbha st. 1): the mere combination of the 9th and 10th lords gives no particular yoga.
The Sun and Mars in the 8th bring sorrow in their periods (BR Kumbha st. 3); Jupiter in the lagna with Saturn in the 2nd gives mixed results in Jupiter dasa and none in Saturn's (st. 4).
Saturn as lagna lord also owns the 12th, so it is weaker in the 12th (Verma; Frawley p. 162).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
lagna_or_context_notes: Aquarius is a biped sign, strong as lagna (Brihat Jataka 1.17). Frawley calls Aquarius sometimes the worst ascendant for worldly fame because the lagna lord also owns the 12th, yet the best for spiritual growth (p. 162).

summary: Pisces rising is classically read as learned, grateful, kind to friends, fond of the spouse, fortunate and able to overcome enemies, with a well-proportioned body and good eyes; moderns add emotion, imagination, devotion and dependence on others. The Moon (5th lord) and Mars (2nd and 9th lord) are the good planets and Mars with Jupiter gives yoga; Saturn, Venus, the Sun and Mercury are counted as difficult.
common_outcomes: Learned, grateful, overcomes enemies, fortunate (PD 9.12; JP 9.109).
Well-proportioned shining body and very good eyes (PD 9.12).
Kind to friends and fond of the spouse (PD 9.12; JP 9.109).
Religious, devotional and sensitive (HJH; Frawley).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 9.12: gains by trading pearls and sea products; drinks much water.
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Meena st. 4): Jupiter in the 5th gives more daughters than sons.
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Meena st. 12-14): the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter and Saturn in their own signs and the Moon and Mars exalted form a great yoga, even if one or two are missing.

by_area.personality: Learned, grateful, kind to friends, spirited and strong (PD 9.12; JP 9.109); stubborn, psychically receptive, highly religious, stoical, reserved, just, lacking self-confidence (HJH); emotional, imaginative, impressionable, compassionate, may lack boundaries (Frawley pp. 124-125).
by_area.career: Gains from pearls and sea produce (PD 9.12); ambitious to rule over others but rarely realises it (HJH); good followers and promoters, musicians (Frawley p. 125). Jupiter, lord of the lagna and 10th, in the 10th gives Raja Yoga (BR Meena st. 11).
by_area.finance: Possesses much corn and wealth (JP 9.109); frugal (HJH); the Moon in the 2nd with Mars in the 5th gives wealth in Moon dasa (BR Meena st. 5); the Moon in the 12th loses wealth (st. 2).
by_area.health: Drinks water excessively (PD 9.12); sensitive digestion and nerves, emotional disorders, can depend on sugar or alcohol (Frawley p. 125).
by_area.relationships: Fond of his wife (PD 9.12); can become dependent or make others dependent (Frawley p. 125).
by_area.family: More daughters and few sons if Jupiter is in the 5th (BR Meena st. 4); generally dependent on others through life yet independent in spirit (HJH).
by_area.spirituality: Highly religious, God-fearing, rigid in observance (HJH); loves ceremony, ritual and devotion (Frawley p. 125).

strengtheners: Mars with Jupiter gives yoga (BPHS 34.43-44; LP); Mars with the Moon or Jupiter gives Raja Yoga (HPA).
Mars and Jupiter in exchange (9th and 10th) form a very powerful Raja Yoga; the Moon in the 10th with Jupiter exalted in the 5th is also powerful (Verma).
Saturn in the 12th is good (BR Meena st. 2); Mercury, Jupiter, the Moon and Mars in the 4th give kingly fame in their periods (st. 9-10).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saturn, 11th and 12th lord, is the most harmful (Santhanam; Frawley p. 160).
Venus in the 12th gives no yoga for Pisces or Aquarius (BR Meena st. 1).
The yoga of Saturn in the 12th is reduced in the Moon's sub-period of Jupiter dasa (BR Meena st. 3).
Mars with Mercury, and Mercury with Jupiter, are spoilt combinations (Verma).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
lagna_or_context_notes: For Pisces the lagna lord Jupiter also owns the 10th, giving it double angular lordship; BPHS still treats Jupiter as very favourable here (Santhanam: next to Mars), while HJH and PVR call it neutral.
